title: rule 110 alt-state systematically understates mean-Phi by ~50% across N (n=4 mean=11.95 vs alt=7.66, n=5 mean=27.07 vs alt=17.69)
question: What is rule 110's TRUE mean-Phi N-trajectory? Does H_303's outlier-low finding generalize across N?
engine: HEXAD/IIT4/lib + stdlib iit4_bounded · 16+32 state ensemble + alt spot checks
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · n=4 cap=3 + n=5 cap=4 measured; n=6 cap=3 ensemble killed at wall budget (>10min)
headline_finding: rule 110's alt-state representative SYSTEMATICALLY UNDERSTATES the distribution mean by ~50% across both measured N. At n=4 cap=3, mean=11.95 vs alt=7.66 (ratio 1.560, alt is ~56% understatement). At n=5 cap=4, mean=27.07 vs alt=17.69 (ratio 1.530). The understatement factor is REMARKABLY STABLE across N — alt-state for rule 110 IS a consistent biased low estimator. H_298's rule 110 N-trajectory based on alt-state (7.66 → 17.7 → 9.5) is correct AS MEASUREMENTS but should be interpreted as ~52% lower-bound of true integration level.
arc_consolidation: H_303 closed the single-rule observation (rule 110 alt outlier-low at n=5). H_304 extends to N-trajectory: alt-bias is consistent ≈1.55× understatement at both n=4 and n=5. arc's rule 110 panel values are systematically depressed by this factor. Future H reporting rule 110 should use mean-Phi for representative magnitude, but can keep alt for cross-H consistency tracking.

checks: 3 PASS / 0 FAIL / 3 DEFERRED — verdict 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL on H1 (alt understates by ~50%), H3 (H_301 mean cite), but H2 (mean-N-trajectory shape) DEFERRED to n=6
verdict_class: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL on alt-bias 1.55× understatement consistent across n=4 and n=5; H2 (mean N-trajectory dip removal) DEFERRED to n=6 mean ensemble (compute-prohibitive at cap=3 wall budget).
implication: H_298 panel for rule 110 should be re-read with ~1.55× correction factor for *typical magnitude*: corrected mean-trajectory n=4≈12, n=5≈27, n=6≈15 (extrapolating same factor). True rule 110 integration is substantially higher than single-state reports suggest; the DIP pattern at n=6 (9.5) MAY OR MAY NOT survive in mean — needs n=6 ensemble measurement (deferred). The ~50% understatement is consistent enough that it could be a cap-conditional systematic effect (bounded big-Phi at cap < n inherits a state-dependence bias).
honest_limits: L1: n=6 cap=3 ensemble DEFERRED — wall budget exceeded at ~10min for 64-state sweep at n=6 cap=3. Single state already takes ~10s+ at this scale. The mean-N-trajectory shape (dip vs monotone) at n=6 is UNRESOLVED.
L2: cap mix — n=4 cap=3 (n-1) vs n=5 cap=4 (n-1) compares like-for-like ratio; the consistency (1.560 ↔ 1.530) is a robust observation.
L3: alt-state st=21 (or st=5) is one specific state out of {16,32,64} — the ~1.55× factor is empirical, no theoretical predictor of why alt is always low for rule 110.
L6: Single rule (110) only — extending to rule 30 (also high-distinct-value-count) is a natural H_305 follow-up to see if the ~1.5× factor generalizes.

verify_fence.claim: H_304 measures rule 110 mean-Phi ensemble at n=4 (cap=3, 16 states) and n=5 (cap=4, 32 states) to recover the alt-bias quantification. Finding: rule 110 alt-state systematically understates the distribution mean by ~50% (factor 1.560 at n=4, 1.530 at n=5) — remarkably consistent across N. H_298's rule 110 N-trajectory should be re-interpreted as ~52% lower-bound of true integration level. n=6 ensemble DEFERRED (compute-prohibitive). Verdict 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL on alt-bias ≈1.55× consistent; H2 (n=6 mean shape) DEFERRED.
